title: Module-object and ringed-topos derived tensor comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism and $\Lambda$ a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Work on representatives of the small pro-étale sites small relative to the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_T=\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, for $T=X,Y$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and also denote by $R_T$ its section-ring sheaf. Let
$$E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$$
be the equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], preserving the underlying abelian sheaf. On the left use relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor], total derived tensor and the module-object functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]; on the right use the sheaf-module derived constructions of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Flat means that tensor with the object is exact, and K-flat means that its direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic complex is acyclic, with the internal-module and sheaf-module definitions [pur713-def-kflat-module, def-pc-kflat-complex].
The equivalence $E_T$ is additive, exact and symmetric monoidal for the specified relative tensors, preserves and reflects flat objects and K-flat complexes, and identifies total tensor complexes, K-flat derived tensors and their units. Its induced equivalence $D(E_T)$ identifies the total derived module-object pullback and pushforward with ringed-topos $Lf^*$ and $Rf_*$ for $f^{-1}R_Y\xrightarrow{\alpha_f}R_X$, including the specified derived adjunction, its unit, counit and pullback composition comparisons. The underived identification of pullback is $f^*M=R_X\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y}f^{-1}M$ [def-sfb-module-upper-star]; pushforward is [def-sfb-module-lower-star].
More precisely, under these tensor and functor identifications, the actual oplax tensor map $\delta_f:Lf^*(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)\to Lf^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lf^*N$ induced by the module-object pullback and localization is carried to the canonical ringed-topos tensor isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; its actual lax map $\mu_f$ is carried to $\delta_f^{-1}$. This is equality of these specified natural transformations under the comparison isomorphisms. In particular the module-object proper projection map, the adjoint under $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ of $(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)\circ\delta_{f,Rf_*K,L}$, is carried to the precise ringed-topos projection map $\alpha_{K,L}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], rather than just some map between its endpoints. For an open immersion $j$, the equivalences also identify levelwise module extension by zero and its adjunction $D(j_!)\dashv Lj^*$ with ringed-topos extension by zero and restriction, including their unit and counit and the $\mu_j$ used in the adjoint-of-unit open projection map.
